correctness.rationale: The graph has n>=4 cyclic rungs, vertical/horizontal edges and one lower-to-next-upper diagonal. State alphabet 0,A,B, allowed neighboring transitions, and the stated domination constraints at empty center produce exactly the displayed six pair states and 10 allowed edges. Independently constructed characteristic determinant t[t^5-2zt^3-z^2t^2-z^2t-z^2], with cycle weights z on occupied new columns; Z_n=tr(T^n) follows from closed-walk bijection. Checked each of 10 edges against both integer potential inequalities, giving |I|>=ceil(2n/5) and <=floor(2n/3). Equality cycles are uniquely periods five and three, with 5/3 shifts when divisibility permits; concatenations of 2-, 3-, 5-cycles attain rounded bounds for all n>=4. Positive-activity transfer is irreducible with 2- and 3-cycles, so primitive; simple positive Perron root is analytic. Implicit function theorem in z^(1/5) and z^(-1/3), respectively, produces the claimed root and density coefficients 2/5,2/25,2/3,-2/9. Independently enumerated all vertex subsets for n=4..10, compared exact Z_n polynomials and bounds; finite check corroborates, not proves infinite n.

These specific answers are not implied by the generic transfer-matrix method alone without a new local-state analysis. No paper-sized general theorem is required for this self-contained exact family.
